items.q: After engine.say('Hello') and before engine.runAndWait(), what has a pyttsx3 engine done?
options: It has spoken the text and is waiting for the next line
It has only queued the text; nothing is spoken yet
It has raised an error because the queue is not running
rationales: say() does not speak; with the dummy driver the list of events was still empty after it.
No error is raised; the text simply waits in the queue.

items.q: In pyttsx3 2.99, what does engine.say('') do?
options: It queues a moment of silence
It raises ValueError
It queues nothing and returns an error message
rationales: Nothing is queued for an empty text.
It returns the message Argument value can't be None or empty and does not raise.

items.q: At the default rate of 200 words per minute, how long does a text of 1,800 words take to speak?
options: 9.0 minutes
0.3 seconds
360.0 minutes
rationales: 0.3 is the seconds per word, not the total.
1,800 / 200 is 9.0; 360 would come from multiplying.

items.q: Which statement about saving speech with pyttsx3 is correct?
options: Every engine writes only WAV, whatever the file name says
The macOS driver writes .aiff, while the eSpeak and SAPI5 drivers write WAV
It writes an MP3 when the file name ends in .mp3
rationales: The chapter says WAV only, but the source of the macOS driver says that Apple writes .aiff, not .wav.
The package cannot save MP3 at all; the file name does not choose the format.

items.q: Under Python 3.14.4, which of these modules can still be imported?
options: aifc
audioop
wave
rationales: aifc was removed in Python 3.13.
audioop was removed in Python 3.13.

items.q: Which Whisper model name is accepted by release 20250625 but is not in the chapter's list?
options: turbo
huge
base-v3
rationales: There is no model named huge.
There is no model named base-v3.

items.q: Besides the Python packages, what must be installed for Whisper to decode an audio file?
options: A sound card driver
The ffmpeg program
The eSpeak engine
rationales: Whisper reads a file; it does not play or record sound.
eSpeak is for pyttsx3's speech, not for Whisper.

items.q: A segment starts at 5.64 seconds. Which is its start time in Whisper's SRT file?
rationales: That is the VTT form, without hours and with a full stop.
That is the TSV form, in milliseconds.

items.q: Which line is the VTT form of the SRT time 00:00:05,640?
rationales: VTT uses a full stop before the milliseconds, not a comma.
The milliseconds need three digits.

items.q: Why does the chapter find the downloaded file with Path().glob('downloaded_content.*')?
options: The extension depends on the audio format that was downloaded
glob is what downloads the file
The outtmpl option cannot contain a file name
rationales: glob only finds files that already exist.
outtmpl can hold a file name; only the extension is left to the format.

items.q: yt-dlp is given the title 'What: is? this/that'. What happens to the colon, question mark and slash in the file name?
options: They are replaced by look-alike characters
They are deleted
The download stops with an error
rationales: The chapter says they are excluded, but yt-dlp 2026.8.19 replaces them.
The download is not refused because of a title.

items.q: Why give speak() the engine as an argument instead of creating it inside?
options: pyttsx3 does not allow a global engine
A recording stand-in can then replace the engine, so the function can be tested without a voice
say() returns the audio, which must be passed on
rationales: Nothing forbids it; the choice is about testing.
say() returns nothing useful; it only queues.
